questions.question: Which core concepts does the tutorial use to explain HTML?
key_answer_facts: Syntax, tags, attributes, and structure.

questions.question: How does the tutorial define syntax?
key_answer_facts: The letters and symbols used to write a language or code.

questions.question: What does the letter A mean in an HTML link tag?
key_answer_facts: It stands for anchor because the word is attached or linked to another site or page location.

questions.question: What are HTML tags according to the tutorial?
key_answer_facts: Repeated symbols combined with letters that identify the type of content to display.

questions.question: Why is the doctype declaration placed on the first line?
key_answer_facts: It tells the browser that the document is an HTML web page.

questions.question: How is a closing tag distinguished from an opening tag?
key_answer_facts: A forward slash follows the less-than symbol in the closing tag.

questions.question: Where should visible page content be placed?
key_answer_facts: Inside the body tag.

questions.question: How are attributes related to tags?
key_answer_facts: Attributes describe content and are attached to and placed inside tags.

questions.question: How does the tutorial compare a website structure to a person?
key_answer_facts: A website has a head, body, and footer like a person has a head, body, and feet.

questions.question: What roles do the head, body, and footer serve?
key_answer_facts: The head describes what the site is about.
The body contains what visitors see.
The footer often summarizes the site content.

questions.question: Why does HTML structure make coding easier?
key_answer_facts: It organizes code into manageable sections and prevents overwhelm.

What is amyloidosis?
key_answer_facts: A disease caused by tissue damage from deposits of abnormally folded proteins.

questions.question: How does the body normally handle an incorrectly folded protein?
key_answer_facts: Proteases identify and chop it into small pieces.

questions.question: How can protein production lead to amyloid buildup?
key_answer_facts: Normal proteins may be overproduced so some misfold.
Abnormal proteins with incorrect amino-acid sequences may be produced and misfold.

questions.question: What structure forms when amyloid proteins clump outside the cell?
key_answer_facts: A rigid insoluble beta sheet that deposits in extracellular tissue.

questions.question: What distinguishes systemic from localized amyloidosis?
key_answer_facts: Systemic deposits occur across multiple organ systems.
Localized deposits occur in one organ.

questions.question: Which protein is misfolded in AL amyloidosis?
key_answer_facts: Immunoglobulin light chains.

questions.question: Why can prolonged inflammation cause AA amyloidosis?
key_answer_facts: The liver releases much serum amyloid A during inflammation.
A portion misfolds and accumulates in tissues.

questions.question: How can kidney amyloid deposits eventually cause edema?
key_answer_facts: Podocyte damage lets albumin spill into urine.
Lower blood protein reduces oncotic pressure and moves water into tissues.

questions.question: How can amyloid damage the heart?
key_answer_facts: It can stiffen the heart walls and cause restrictive cardiomyopathy.
It can disrupt electrical conduction and cause arrhythmias.

questions.question: How do amyloid plaques harm the brain in Alzheimer disease?
key_answer_facts: They interfere with neuron signaling.
They weaken blood-vessel walls and can trigger inflammation that damages neurons.

questions.question: How does biopsy staining identify amyloid?
key_answer_facts: Congo red makes amyloid pink.
Under polarized light it appears apple green.

questions.question: Which medication removes amyloid deposits?
questions.reason: The transcript says no effective removal method and names no medication.

questions.question: What is the five-year survival rate for AL amyloidosis?
Which genetic test confirms amyloidosis?
Which diet prevents amyloid deposits?
Why can freely licensed media not simply be reused without conditions?
key_answer_facts: The license grants specific permission whose terms must be respected.

questions.question: Why is crediting only Wikipedia or Wikimedia Commons incorrect?
key_answer_facts: The individual creator made the work and deserves credit.

questions.question: What must a reuser check for each media file?
key_answer_facts: The requested attribution and the specific license.

questions.question: Why can Google help locate Wiki Loves Africa photographs?
key_answer_facts: Google indexes Commons, where the competition photographs are freely licensed.

questions.question: What information does the Commons file page provide for the example photograph?
key_answer_facts: A description, the creator credit, and the license.

questions.question: What is the minimum attribution required for the example photograph?
key_answer_facts: Name the author and the precise license including its version.

questions.question: Why should an attribution mention the license?
key_answer_facts: It tells others they may reuse the work under the same terms.

questions.question: How do hyperlinks improve an attribution?
key_answer_facts: They can lead readers to Commons and to the Creative Commons license explanation.

questions.question: What does the ideal attribution include?
key_answer_facts: The author.
A linked license with version.
A link to the exact Commons file page.

questions.question: Why is linking the exact Commons file useful?
key_answer_facts: It lets readers find and download the exact high-resolution source for reuse or modification.

questions.question: What is the consequence of using a freely licensed photo without attribution?
key_answer_facts: It violates copyright and breaks the law.

questions.question: How much does Wikimedia charge to download a photograph?
When does a Creative Commons license expire?
Which country has the strictest attribution law?
Does fair use eliminate every attribution requirement?
What new RAIDZ capability does the tutorial demonstrate?
key_answer_facts: Expanding an existing RAIDZ vdev by adding one disk.

questions.question: What size must a disk have to be eligible for RAIDZ expansion?
key_answer_facts: It must be the same size as or larger than the existing drives.

questions.question: Why does a larger added disk not immediately provide its extra capacity?
key_answer_facts: RAIDZ drives conform to the size of the smallest drive so the layout remains symmetrical.

questions.question: Can adding disks change a RAIDZ1 vdev into RAIDZ2?
key_answer_facts: No; expansion widens the vdev but its RAIDZ type remains fixed from creation.

questions.question: How does the interface start a RAIDZ expansion?
key_answer_facts: Open Manage Devices, select the RAIDZ vdev, click Extend, and select an eligible disk.

questions.question: Why must the system write to a newly added drive?
key_answer_facts: It must create parity on the new drive while leaving existing data in place.

questions.question: How does expansion affect the stripe width of old and new data?
key_answer_facts: Old data retains its original three-drive stripe width.
New data is written with a four-drive stripe width.

questions.question: How does the ZFS in-place rebalancing script redistribute data?
key_answer_facts: It copies files, creates another copy, and copies them back so data is refreshed across the expanded drives.

questions.question: Why can a later expansion take time?
key_answer_facts: It is CPU intensive because parity must be recalculated.
Duration depends on how much data is present.

questions.question: Why can an extremely wide vdev be difficult to maintain?
key_answer_facts: Resilvering a failed drive requires pulling data across all of the drives.

questions.question: Can the demonstrated feature convert a mirror into RAIDZ?
key_answer_facts: No, mirror-to-RAIDZ conversion is not available.

What is the purpose of the 1Lib1Ref campaign?
key_answer_facts: It encourages librarians, archivists, and information professionals to learn Wikipedia editing and add a reference to improve article quality.

questions.question: Why are information professionals suited to improve Wikipedia references?
key_answer_facts: They have access to quality sources such as books, journals, periodicals, and newspapers.

questions.question: How can a contributor find an article needing a citation?
key_answer_facts: Browse for unsourced statements, use problem-article lists, or use Citation Hunt.

questions.question: What should a contributor put in the edit summary?
key_answer_facts: The 1Lib1Ref project hashtag so the project receives credit.

questions.question: How does Citation Hunt choose content to show?
key_answer_facts: It randomly selects an article carrying a citation-needed flag.

questions.question: How can the editing interface generate a citation from a source URL?
key_answer_facts: Paste the URL into the automatic citation generator and insert the generated citation.

questions.question: What event format can an institution host for the campaign?
key_answer_facts: An in-person, online, or hybrid drop-in editathon.

questions.question: How can an institution make a citation event easier to attend?
key_answer_facts: Pair it with a familiar break or part of the workday, such as coffee or lunch.

questions.question: How can an institution use its own collections during an event?
key_answer_facts: Use unique collections, archives, finding aids, or guides as citation sources and pair them with curated article lists.

questions.question: How can the campaign help reduce gender bias in references?
key_answer_facts: Add citations authored by women and use curated Citation Hunt lists focused on gender topics.

questions.question: What tool tracks institutional participation in greater detail?
key_answer_facts: The Wikimedia Foundation Labs dashboard.

Which citation style is mandatory for every campaign edit?
questions.reason: No single citation style is mandated.

questions.question: How many edits did the campaign receive last year?
questions.reason: No annual edit total is given.

questions.question: Does Citation Hunt verify that every source is academically peer reviewed?
What did the student work on the Women in Government article demonstrate?
key_answer_facts: Students improved a high-traffic article whose US section had focused mostly on politicians as babies.

questions.question: Why was the National Women Studies Association a good partner?
key_answer_facts: Its mission promotes knowledge about women and gender and accurate public scholarship, aligning with Wikipedia work.

questions.question: What impact did the spring 2015 women studies courses have?
key_answer_facts: Five courses involved about 200 students.
They improved about 100 articles that received 4.4 million views.

questions.question: Why does the program flag classes with more than fifty students?
key_answer_facts: Instructors may struggle to train the students and monitor all their Wikipedia work.

questions.question: How much time should significant Wikipedia assignments receive?
key_answer_facts: At least six weeks because students need several weeks to learn and become comfortable editing.

questions.question: How does the dashboard explain a student editor's course context to other editors?
key_answer_facts: It automatically adds a course template to the student user page.
It updates course and article talk pages from dashboard actions.

questions.question: What recurring learning sequence did the successful behavioral ecology course use?
key_answer_facts: Students read about a skill, practice it, and then deploy it.

questions.question: Why was the expert editing pilot judged a poor return?
key_answer_facts: Participants produced only five and three-quarter printed pages after sixty hours of staff time.

questions.question: What did the high-achieving student pilot learn about voluntary editing?
key_answer_facts: Only two of forty-four students made good contributions.
Most students were too busy to edit outside class despite enthusiasm.

questions.question: How does the Visiting Scholars program benefit editors and libraries?
key_answer_facts: Editors receive remote access to high-quality research materials.
Libraries increase the impact of their collections while contributing to public knowledge.

questions.question: What kinds of assignments are described as Wikipedia policy problems?
key_answer_facts: Assignments using original research, group accounts, or substantial off-wiki work.

questions.question: What annual salary does a Wikipedia content expert receive?
Which learning management system integrates with the dashboard?
questions.reason: No learning management system is named.

questions.question: What percentage of student edits survive for five years?
questions.reason: No five-year retention statistic is given.
